issues.legal_issue: A later writ petition challenging an award may be barred where the award challenge was omitted from earlier related proceedings and the later challenge is brought after substantial unexplained delay.
material_facts: The landowners had unsuccessfully challenged the acquisition and were given liberty to make a representation about release of the land.
An award had been made before the landowners brought their second set of writ petitions, but those petitions challenged only the rejection of their representation and did not challenge the award.
The second set of proceedings also failed, with the rejection of the representation upheld by the Supreme Court.
The landowners first challenged the award in a fresh writ petition filed in 2004, after the earlier proceedings had concluded.
issues.conclusion: The fresh writ petition was not maintainable because the award challenge was barred by Order II Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure and by laches and delay.
issues.legal_principle: Order II Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure bars a later suit or proceeding where a claim that could have been raised in an earlier proceeding arising from the relevant cause was omitted; a challenge brought after substantial unexplained delay may also be barred by laches. The Court applied these principles because the award existed during the earlier proceedings in which the landowners challenged only the rejection of their representation.

rule.if: later_writ_petition and prior_acquisition_challenge_lost and representation_challenge_lost and award_claim_omitted_in_prior_petition and substantial_unexplained_delay

predicates.later_writ_petition: The claim is brought in a later writ petition challenging an award.
predicates.prior_acquisition_challenge_lost: The claimants previously challenged the acquisition and that challenge failed.
predicates.representation_challenge_lost: The claimants later challenged the rejection of a representation concerning the acquired land, and that challenge failed.
predicates.award_claim_omitted_in_prior_petition: The award existed during the earlier related petition, but the claimants did not challenge it in that petition.
predicates.substantial_unexplained_delay: The claimants waited a substantial period to bring the award challenge without explaining the delay.

issues.definition: When claimants bring a later writ petition after losing related acquisition and representation challenges, omit an available award challenge from the earlier petition, and then delay substantially without explanation, the later petition is not maintainable.

issues.legal_issue: The prescribed time limit for making an award does not cause an acquisition to lapse after possession has been taken under an urgency procedure.
material_facts: The acquisition proceeded under an urgency provision that dispensed with objections.
The acquisition was upheld in the earlier challenge.
Possession of the acquired land was taken before the award was made.
The award was made after possession had been taken.
issues.conclusion: The award-timing provision did not apply after possession had been taken under the urgency provision, so the acquisition did not lapse because the award was made later.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 17(1) and 11A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, once possession is taken under Section 17(1), Section 11A is not attracted and the acquisition does not lapse for failure to make an award within its prescribed period. The Court relied on Satendra Prasad Jain v. State of Uttar Pradesh, affirmed in Awadh Bihari Yadav v. State of Bihar.

predicates.land_acquisition_case: The proceeding concerns the acquisition of land.
predicates.urgency_procedure_invoked: The acquiring authority proceeded under a procedure permitting urgency-based acquisition.
predicates.possession_taken_before_award: The acquiring authority took possession of the land before making the award.

issues.definition: In a land-acquisition case, when an urgency procedure is used and possession is taken before the award, a delayed award does not cause the acquisition to lapse.
